## comic_book_panel_page

> Multi-panel American comic-book interior page with speech balloons, halftone shading, and short panel captions.

**Artifact:** `comic_page`, `1024x1536`, aspect `2:3`
**Demo vars:** `templates/comic_book/_vars_examples/comic_book_panel_page.yml`

### English

```
[1. Subject] A single interior comic-book page from the fictional series "Bristolwood Press: Night Wire", page 07, drawn in American comic-book style. The page contains between four and six panels reading left-to-right, top-to-bottom, telling a short connected beat described by panel captions the courier sprints across a rain-slick rooftop, she skids to a halt at the antenna, and a gloved hand seizes her shoulder from behind. Characters wear original costumes with no real-franchise IP.
[2. Action] Across the panels the action progresses from a setup beat to a pivot beat to a payoff beat: panel 1 — the courier sprints across a rain-slick rooftop; panel 2 — she skids to a halt at the antenna; panel 3 — a gloved hand seizes her shoulder from behind; additional panels (if 4-6 grid) hold reaction shots and a final silent landing panel. Speech balloons carry short, declarative English dialogue; thought balloons distinguished by scalloped tails.
[3. Scene] The story unfolds inside the world of "Bristolwood Press: Night Wire". Backgrounds are rendered in flat-color blocks with halftone midtones, never photoreal. Each panel earns a distinct camera angle — wide establishing, over-shoulder, low hero angle, tight close-up — to build pacing rhythm.
[4. Composition] Vertical 2:3 page. A 4-6 panel grid; suggested layout: row 1 holds one wide establishing panel; row 2 holds two equal panels; row 3 holds two stacked or staggered panels; row 4 holds one final payoff panel. Gutters are 12-16px white channels with crisp ink borders. Page-number tag "07" sits in a small bottom corner box. Speech balloons placed to read in the same direction as the panel order; tails point unambiguously to the speaker.
[5. Style] American comic-book interior aesthetic — bold inked outlines with brush-weighted line variation, four-color halftone shading, solid black shadow accents, dense Ben-Day dots in midtones. Speech balloons drawn with crisp 1-pixel borders and a clean US-comic letterform set in upper-case. No manga screen-tone, no anime cel-shading, no painterly watercolor, no 3D-CG, no photoreal backgrounds.

Text to render exactly (chunked into named slots):
- page_no: "page 07"
- panel1_caption: "the courier sprints across a rain-slick rooftop"
- panel2_caption: "she skids to a halt at the antenna"
- panel3_caption: "a gloved hand seizes her shoulder from behind"

Preserve (edit mode only):
- panel grid gutters
- speech balloon tail direction
- inked outline weight
- halftone dot pattern

NO: manga screen-tone, anime cel-shading, painterly watercolor, photoreal rendering, 3D-CG model render, real Marvel or DC trade dress, real-publisher logos, real superhero likenesses, branded character costume IP, storyboard pencil sketch look, inconsistent character design between panels
```

## comic_book_variant_cover

> Single-figure American comic-book variant cover with masthead, issue number, and credit slug, in bold inks and halftone.

**Artifact:** `poster`, `1024x1536`, aspect `2:3`
**Demo vars:** `templates/comic_book/_vars_examples/comic_book_variant_cover.yml`

### English

```
[1. Subject] A single hero figure on a variant cover for the fictional comic series "STARFALL PATROL", issue 017, drawn by J. Marquez (Atlas Comics). The figure dominates the frame in a confident late-90s prestige hero pose — three-quarter stance, weight on back foot, gaze cutting toward the upper-left masthead. Costume reads as an original design with no real-franchise iconography.
[2. Action] The figure is captured at the apex of a beat — cape mid-snap, fist half-clenched, hair lifting against an off-screen wind. There is no panel grid; the entire 2:3 surface acts as a single dramatic cover plate. Tiny secondary motion lines around the figure imply pressure rather than illustrate it.
[3. Scene] A flat, graphic backdrop calibrated to support the figure: a single bold halftone color field, broken by one or two angular shape bands of a complementary tone. No photographic environment, no rendered cityscape — the cover treats the page as poster, not as window. Subtle four-color halftone dot pattern reads in the midtones.
[4. Composition] Vertical 2:3 page. Title masthead "STARFALL PATROL" runs across the top ~12% of the frame in a heavy display letterform. Issue number "017" sits as a small badge in the upper-right corner. The figure occupies the central 70% of the frame. Cover-artist credit "J. Marquez (Atlas Comics)" sits in a thin slug along the bottom edge, ~3% tall, left-justified. Generous margin of bleed-safe space on all four edges.
[5. Style] American comic-book cover aesthetic in the late-90s prestige register of the deep crimson, ink black, off-white, gold spot family. Bold inked outlines with brush-weighted line variation, four-color halftone shading, dense Ben-Day dots in midtones, solid black for shadow accents. Saturated but limited palette — never neon. Display masthead set in a heavy comic serif/sans hybrid letterform; issue number set in a tight numeric slab. No anime line art, no manga screen-tone, no painterly softness, no photoreal rendering.

Text to render exactly (chunked into named slots):
- title_logo: "STARFALL PATROL"
- issue_no: "#017"
- cover_artist_credit: "cover by J. Marquez (Atlas Comics)"

Preserve (edit mode only):
- bold inked outline weight
- halftone dot pattern
- masthead letterform

NO: manga screen-tone, anime cel-shading, photoreal rendering, painterly soft edges, lens flare, real Marvel or DC trade dress, real-publisher logos, real superhero likenesses, branded character costume IP, watermarks
```
